You can finish setting up later from the Home screen. It\'s easier to follow these steps now, especially the first time.

Once you enable Android’s Accessibility button and choose an app or app shortcut, you can open it while using other apps. The button belongs to Android itself. It may appear in the navigation bar or float at the edge of your screen, depending on your device and settings.
Accessibility button at the bottom right of Android’s navigation bar
Accessibility button floating at the right edge of the screen

Android needs you to switch it on in Accessibility settings. Look for \"Accessibility Button Launcher\" and turn it on. On some phones, like Samsung, you\'ll need to tap \"Installed apps\" first to find it.
Choose an app, or a specific action inside an app.
Some phones put background apps to sleep, which can stop the button from working. Allowing unrestricted battery use prevents that.
Press the accessibility button any time to open your app. You can revisit these steps from the Home screen.
Xiaomi phones need one more step. You\'ll find it in the checklist on the Home screen.
Keep the service alive in the background
Allow the app to ignore battery optimization so the shortcut keeps working reliably when the app is in the background.

Your Xiaomi device is more aggressive about killing background apps. Allow the app to ignore battery optimization, then lock the app from the recent apps switcher so the shortcut keeps working reliably.

Open the recent apps switcher, find Accessibility Button Launcher, and press the lock icon so MIUI keeps it alive in the background. You\'ll know it\'s done correctly if a lock icon displays next to the app name in the app switcher.
I locked the app in recents
Use this screen for questions about choosing what the button opens, troubleshooting, and background behavior.

Can the button open an app shortcut instead of an app?
Yes. In the picker, switch to App shortcuts. The button opens one thing, an app or an app shortcut, and choosing one replaces the other.
Why is the app shortcut I want missing?

Only shortcuts that apps publish for everyone are listed. Shortcuts an app creates for you, or that you pinned, can\'t be listed. Some apps also keep their shortcuts private to the launcher, so this app can\'t open them and they are hidden.
The service listens for the system Accessibility trigger and launches only the app you select. It does not add automation or overlays.

I don\'t see the accessibility button: Check that the service is enabled. Some devices hide the button depending on navigation mode, but the Accessibility shortcut can still work. On Xiaomi devices, the button may not appear immediately after enabling the service in system settings. If that happens, lock the screen once and unlock it again so MIUI refreshes the shortcut button.
Pressing the button does nothing: Return here and confirm the service is still enabled and something is assigned to the button.
My selected app no longer opens: Choose the app again. Its launcher entry may have changed or the app may be disabled.

On Xiaomi and some other devices, aggressive battery and background restrictions can stop the accessibility service from staying active after the app is backgrounded. Finish the battery and recents lock steps in the Home checklist if your device needs them.
